analysis.one_liner: Union Bank of India is a government-owned public sector bank that takes deposits and lends to corporates, retail borrowers, agriculture and MSMEs across India.
analysis.whats_happening: Union Bank's board meets on 19 October 2026 - tomorrow - to approve Q2 FY27 (July-September 2026) results, with an earnings call the same afternoon, so the market has not yet seen this quarter's numbers. The last reported quarter, Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026), showed standalone net profit up about 30% year-on-year to ₹5,332 crore from ₹4,116 crore, with gross NPA improving to 2.65% from 3.52% and ROE at 17.23%. In the quarter before that (Q4 FY26, to March 2026), profit rose too but net interest margin slipped to 2.64% from 2.87% a year earlier, and the stock fell about 6% on results day as that margin pressure overshadowed the headline profit growth.
analysis.plain_terms: This is one of India's largest government-run banks - the Government of India owns roughly three-quarters of it. The core tension right now: profit keeps rising, but it is increasingly being helped by fewer bad-loan writeoffs (asset quality is genuinely improving) rather than the bank earning more on every rupee it lends, since the gap between what it pays depositors and earns from borrowers (net interest margin) has been shrinking. The stock trades cheap on paper - roughly 6.5-7 times earnings and close to its book value - partly because PSU banks have historically earned lower, less consistent returns than private banks, and partly because the government periodically sells down its stake to raise capital, which dilutes existing shareholders.
analysis.quarters: FY26 (year to March 2026) net profit was ₹18,697 crore, with full-year ROA 1.25% and ROE 15.86%. Q4 FY26 profit grew 6.6% YoY to ₹5,316 crore, but NIM fell to 2.64% from 2.87% a year earlier - management flagged margin pressure from competition for deposits. Q1 FY27 (June 2026) then showed profit up ~30% YoY to ₹5,332 crore, ROA 1.36%, ROE 17.23%, and a sharp improvement in gross NPA to 2.65% from 3.52%. Note this profit jump is helped significantly by falling credit costs/recoveries rather than confirmed NII expansion - the NIM trend from the prior quarter had not yet reversed as of the last confirmed data point. A separate report cited provisional Q2 FY27 gross advances growth of ~18.5% YoY, but this appears to be a pre-results business update, not the audited figures due tomorrow - treat it as unconfirmed until the board-approved results land.
analysis.performance_read: The stock has strongly outperformed recently: up 27.33% over 1 year versus Nifty -9.53% and peer CANBK -4.07%, and up 318.51% over 5 years versus Nifty +25.27% and peer +251.25%. The stock is still 40.9% below its October 2010 peak of ₹290.64 - but that peak is 16 years old, predates the PSU banking NPA crisis of the mid-2010s, and there is no corporate action (no splits, no demerger) distorting the price series, so this is a genuine long-run drawdown rather than an artifact. The more relevant recent range is the 52-week band of ₹132.77-196.47; at ₹171.68 the stock sits roughly in the middle of that range, well off its 52-week high.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 6.5-7x earnings and about 1-1.1x book value, the stock is cheap next to private bank peers (often cited around 10x). Why it is cheap: PSU banks carry a structural discount for government control, historically lower and more volatile returns, and the overhang of periodic government stake sales (a 2024 QIP already cut the government's holding from ~77% to 74.76%). Whether it is cheap given current fundamentals is a separate question - ROE has recently run at 15-17%, which is strong for a PSU bank, and capital adequacy (CRAR 18.10%, CET-1 15.69% as of March 2026) is comfortable, reducing near-term dilution risk. The discount may reflect legacy PSU-bank skepticism more than today's numbers.
analysis.growth_read: Profit growth over the last two reported quarters has been real, but it leans on asset-quality recoveries (falling provisions as GNPA/NNPA improve) more than on expanding lending margins - NIM was still compressing as of the last confirmed quarter (Q4 FY26). That makes recent growth look more margin-recovery-led than volume-led on the profitability side, even if loan book growth itself has likely continued; this is less durable than growth coming from both volumes and margins rising together.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into capital, not just paper gains: CRAR of 18.10% and CET-1 of 15.69% (March 2026) are comfortable buffers, and gross/net NPAs have fallen sharply (GNPA 3.52%→2.65%, NNPA to 0.47% YoY as of June 2026). The more relevant risk here is business risk - margin compression in a competitive deposit market - rather than financial or credit risk, since asset quality and capital levels both look healthy on the data available.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India is the promoter, holding 74.76% of the bank - unchanged since a February 2024 QIP that raised ₹3,000 crore and diluted the government stake from about 77% to 74.76%. Promoter pledging, in the sense that applies to private company promoters, is not applicable here since the promoter is the sovereign. Foreign institutional investors hold roughly 8.6% and domestic institutions roughly 12%, per recent shareholding data. Not verified - check Screener for which specific institutional or marquee investors are on the register; no individual well-known investor name could be confirmed from available sources.
strengths: Gross NPA fell to 2.65% in Q1 FY27 from 3.52% a year earlier, with net NPA down to 0.47% - a clear, multi-quarter asset-quality improvement
ROE reached 17.23% in Q1 FY27, among the stronger recent readings for a PSU bank, up from 15.86% for full-year FY26
Comfortable capital buffers - CRAR 18.10% and CET-1 15.69% as of March 2026 - which lowers the odds of a near-term dilutive capital raise
Dividend per share has risen steadily from ₹1.90 (FY22) to ₹5.00 (FY26), tracking the profit recovery, for a current yield of 2.91%
watchpoints: Net interest margin fell to 2.64% in Q4 FY26 from 2.87% a year earlier - the market punished the stock (down ~6% on results day) even as profit rose, because margin compression threatens the durability of profit growth
Q2 FY27 results land 19 October 2026 (tomorrow) - whether NIM stabilizes or keeps sliding is the open question the market hasn't priced yet

As a government-controlled bank, periodic equity dilution is a structural feature, not a one-off - a 2024 QIP already cut the government's stake from ~77% to 74.76%, and further capital raises remain possible
A cited provisional ~18.5% YoY advances growth figure for Q2 FY27 comes from a pre-results business update, not confirmed audited numbers - don't treat it as settled until tomorrow's results
analysis.one_thing: The 19 October 2026 Q2 FY27 results - specifically whether net interest margin holds near 2.64% or slides further, since that determines whether profit growth is still margin-supported or increasingly dependent on lower provisions alone.
analysis.data_notes: FY26 full-year and Q4 FY26 figures (profit ₹18,697 crore, CRAR 18.10%, CET-1 15.69%, Q4 profit ₹5,316 crore, NIM 2.64%) were cross-checked against the bank's own press release and corroborated by independent news coverage. Q1 FY27 figures (profit ₹5,332 crore, ROE 17.23%, GNPA 2.65%) were consistent across multiple independent sources. Discarded conflicting Q2 FY26 (Sep 2025) net profit figures (₹4,426 crore vs ₹4,249 crore reported across different outlets) rather than averaging them, and set aside one search result that appeared to conflate Union Bank of India with the separate, similarly named City Union Bank. Q2 FY27 (September 2026 quarter) results were not yet published at the time of writing - the board meeting is scheduled for tomorrow. Individual institutional/famous-investor names on the shareholding register were not independently verifiable - check Screener.
